messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: High 5xx spike observed in euc2a ingress group. Symptoms: sudden increase in 502/504/connection reset errors from ALB -> Envoy fronting /api and /v1/chat. Alert: avg 5xx rate 18% over 2m, top endpoints: /api/generate, /v1/chat/stream. Impact: customer requests failing, elevated latency. Paging oncall.

pagerduty: Alert acknowledged by jamie (oncall) — ETA 2m. Incident severity: Sev2.

jamie (oncall): I'm on it. Joining call, pulling logs. First glance: Envoy upstream connection resets (RST), increased 5xx from envoy cluster stats. ALB target health shows healthy but high connection resets.

alex (infra): Adding context — earlier today we rolled a target group weight change for euc2a->euc2b for traffic shaping at 08:30UTC. Nothing obvious in LB control plane. Checking NLB/ALB metrics and ENI counts for euc2a.

priya: From runtime side, recent Envoy 1.23.0 config change (conn_keepalive tweak) was rolled to euc2a yesterday. I'm fetching envoy logs now. Might be a config-related regression but could also be network flaps between ALB and envoy.

maya (support): Getting multiple customer reports for 502s, some timed out requests retried. A couple enterprise customers reported errors during heavy batch requests. Updating support triage.

jamie (oncall): Quick mitigation plan: 1) divert portion of traffic away from euc2a (weighted DNS) to euc2b/euc1b. 2) scale up envoy pods in euc2a temporarily. 3) if envoy config suspected, roll back to previous envoy config in euc2a. 4) if network, escalate to cloud provider.

alex (infra): I can do weighted DNS failover via Route53. Suggest shifting 60% of traffic off euc2a to euc2b as a quick mitigation to reduce load and verify. I'll also increase ALB connection timeout to avoid hard RSTs while we triage.

priya: I'll prepare a rollback of the env config. If we see immediate reduction in RSTs after rollback that's telling. Also will try a graceful restart of envoy pods to clear stale connections.

jamie (oncall): Execute steps please. Keep actions in this thread.

alex (infra): Executing Route53 weighted change now — lowering euc2a weight from 100 to 40, increasing euc2b to 60. Route53 change-id: Z3X-apply-7721. Propagation expected ~60s.

deploy-bot: route53: change Z3X-apply-7721 status: PENDING -> INSYNC (timestamp: 1905552550).

maya (support): Noting customers now see partial recovery for some requests, but still elevated errors for long-polling endpoints.

priya: Rolling envoy config back to previous revision (rev 2024-09-30-4) in euc2a. Command:```bash
kubectl -n ingress rollout undo deployment/envoy-ingress -r=2024-09-30-4 --context=euc2a
```Applying now.

deploy-bot: envoy-ingress rollout undo triggered by priya. Job id: rollout-8893.

jamie (oncall): Also scale envoy replicas to handle bursts.

priya: Scaling up:```bash
kubectl -n ingress scale deployment/envoy-ingress --replicas=12 --context=euc2a
```Scaling done at 1905552702.

alex (infra): Increased ALB idle timeout to 120s for target group tg-euc2a to reduce premature resets. API call logs:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:tg-euc2a --attributes Key=idle_timeout.timeout_seconds,Value=120
```
Change applied 1905552735.

priya: envoy rollback complete, pods restarted gracefully. Observing envoy upstream: connection resets dropped from ~1500/s to ~120/s in last 2m. 5xx rate trending down to ~6%.

maya (support): Customer impact: majority of users show improved success rate; still some enterprise batch jobs failing intermittently. Logged customer cases: #CS-3321, #CS-3322.

jamie (oncall): Good. Next: monitor for 15m. If metrics remain stable, we'll keep weighted routing and scale steps until full recovery. If resets persist, cloud provider escalation.

alex (infra): Monitoring NLB and ENI metrics. No obvious AZ-wide network errors (no increased packet drops), but we see elevated connection resets on ALB -> instances only for euc2a. Could be kernel-level ephemeral port exhaustion on envoy hosts. Checking node socket stats.

priya: Checking envoy host tcp stats: netstat shows many TIME_WAIT and some sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on 3 hosts. Kernel tunables look default. If we hit ephemeral port exhaustion under high concurrency, ALB will see RSTs. I'll open ticket to bump ephemeral port range/keepalive on nodes if we confirm.

jamie (oncall): For now, keep DNS weight at 40/60 and scaled replicas. Priya, can you check heap/FD counts and share commands?

priya: Commands I ran to inspect FD counts:```bash
kubectl -n ingress exec -it envoy-pod-abc -- bash -c "ls -l /proc/1/fd | wc -l"
ss -s
cat /proc/net/sockstat
```On the three problematic hosts, FD count ~ 28k, system limit 65k. Not immediate but high. tcp_tw_reuse not enabled.

alex (infra): I'll spin a small ASG rolling update to replace the worst hosts if needed. Creating replacement workers now.

deploy-bot: autoscaling: launched 2 replacement ingress workers in euc2a (instance ids i-0abc, i-0def). Registration to ALB target group in progress.

maya (support): Status page draft: "We are experiencing elevated 5xx errors in euc2a region affecting API requests. Traffic has been shifted to alternate region and mitigations are in place. We will update as we have more info." Leo, can you approve?

leo (product): Approve. Keep wording clear on customer impact and ETA for next update 15m.

jamie (oncall): Quick customer impact summary for post-incident: ~12% of requests in last 30m returned 5xx, primarily in euc2a. Enterprise bulk jobs saw higher failure rates. No data loss. Root cause hypothesis: combination of Envoy config change + high connection churn causing host socket pressure leading to connection resets.

priya: Continued observation — 5xx now ~2.8% and trending down. Replacement hosts healthy and drained old hosts from ALB target group.

alex (infra): Route53 weights remain 40(euc2a)/60(euc2b). If we need to fully failover, plan ready to set euc2a=0.

jamie (oncall): Good. If metrics hold for next 30m, we'll start recovery plan: revert weights back gradually and keep additional replicas until we confirm kernel tunables. Priya, please open a follow-up action for kernel tunables and Envoy config guardrails (alerts on socket counts).

priya: Filed RED-INC-452 follow-up action for kernel tunables, FD monitoring, and an automated Canary for envoy config changes.

maya (support): Customers updated. CS queue reduced. Closing customer-facing updates after next confirmation.

jamie (oncall): Marking incident mitigated for now. Will keep thread open for postmortem notes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident status changed to "mitigated" by jamie at 1905558123.
